_comment: What each distribution publishes, and what to do with it.
This is the input. scripts/build.py reads it, fetches each upstream file,
checks it against the digest here, normalises it, and writes manifest.json
describing both the result and where it came from.
A digest here is the whole of the trust chain's first link: everything the
release publishes is derived from a file that matched one of these, so a
compromised mirror produces a failed build rather than a signed artifact.
Moving a pin means changing url and sha256 together and saying in the
commit message which upstream release it is.
A distribution carries a list of releases. The first is what a plain
install gets and the rest are offered beside it, so the order here is the
offer and not an accident of editing. `branch` is what the package
manager reads as its release and is also what decides whether one release
is an update of another: two builds of `noble` replace each other, while
`resolute` is a different system. So no two releases of one distribution
may share a branch, and scripts/track.py moves each within its own.
Adding a series is deliberate work and never automatic: it means checking
that the app's repositories file is right for it, that its package
manager works under proot on Android and under the ish engine on iOS, and
that the mirror paths the app builds actually resolve.

track.note: 3.22 rather than the newest: 3.23 ships apk-tools 3, whose network fetches fail under proot on Android. See ServerBox's AndroidRootfs.
The previous stable series, kept for anything pinned to its package versions. Same apk-tools 2 as 3.22, so it works under proot.
The tarball is on cdimage and the packages are on archive, so one mirror string cannot name both. follows_mirror is false for that reason.
The previous LTS, and the one most third-party packaging still targets. Ships the same deb822 sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources 26.04 does, so the app writes one file for both.
The dated build, not the .latest. file the same directory offers: that one's bytes change on every rebuild, so a pinned digest would go stale under it.
Same tree layout as 9 — BaseOS, AppStream and CRB under /10/<repo>/aarch64/os/ — so the app's repo file needs only the branch substituted.
